violating.description: The combined divisible-by-15 branch is dropped, so multiples of both 3 and 5 return "fizz" instead of "fizzbuzz".
The multiple-of-3 branch returns the capitalised string "Fizz" instead of "fizz".
The multiple-of-5 test uses n % 10, so odd multiples of 5 such as 5 and 25 fall through and return their number.
The fallthrough returns the integer n instead of its decimal string, so classify(7) returns 7 rather than "7".

preserving.description: Builds the result by concatenating "fizz" and "buzz" and falling back to str(n) when the string is empty, instead of checking 15 first.
Computes the two divisibility flags once, checks both-first with them, and formats the number with %d instead of str().
Uses two-space indentation, blank lines between branches, an f-string for the number, and no trailing newline at end of file.
Uses a lookup table keyed on the two divisibility booleans with str(n) as the default, a different algorithm with the same results.

preserving.description: Writes hello.txt from a quoted heredoc and derives the count from the file itself with awk length().

files.solve.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
cat > hello.txt <<'EOF'
Hello, graderproof!
EOF
awk '{ print length($0) }' hello.txt > count.txt

preserving.description: Writes count.txt before hello.txt, using wc -c on the unterminated greeting and an arithmetic expansion to normalise the number.

files.solve.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
msg="Hello, graderproof!"
len=$(printf '%s' "$msg" | wc -c)
echo $((len)) > count.txt
echo "$msg" > hello.txt
